title: Fee collection without the receipt book: a checklist for school offices
excerpt: Instalments, UPI and cheques, adjustments, defaulters. A practical checklist for running fee collection that the principal can see at a glance.
author: SmartShala team
body:
Fee collection is where a school office spends most of its hours — and where small mistakes cost the most. Here’s a checklist we’d use to set it up properly, whether you run it on paper or in software.

## Before the session starts

- **Write down every fee head.** Tuition, admission, exam, activity, transport — each as its own head, so reports can show where money comes from.
- **Decide the instalments.** Term-wise or quarterly, with due dates set at the start, not chased later.
- **Assign by class, adjust by student.** Most students in a class pay the same; siblings and concessions are exceptions you record, not exceptions you remember.

## Every time a payment comes in

- **Record the mode.** UPI, cheque or demand draft — and the reference number, so it can be reconciled.
- **Issue a receipt immediately**, with a number that never repeats.
- **Post it to the student’s ledger**, so the balance is always current.

## Every week

- **Look at the defaulters list** while it is still short.
- **Send reminders early** — a reminder before the due date gets paid faster than a notice after it.
- **Check cheques that haven’t cleared.**

## At the end of the term

- Compare **collected against expected**, by class.
- Carry balances forward instead of starting new cards.
- Keep the year’s receipts searchable — parents ask for copies.
